text: Engage (संलग्न गराउनु), 5 min: greet students and ask 'What did you see on your way to school today?'. Write responses (paddy field, goat, river, tree, bird, sun, mountain, road, house) on the board without labeling, then ask whether all the things are the same or different to spark curiosity.
source: Exemplar: Components of Environment (reference lesson lp1)
subject: Science

text: Explore (अन्वेषण गर्नु), 10 min: divide students into small groups and give component cards (sunlight, air, water, soil, rice plant, goat, mushroom, bacteria, stone, butterfly). Ask them to sort the cards into two groups by their own understanding while the teacher circulates asking guiding questions.
source: Exemplar: Components of Environment (reference lesson lp1)
subject: Science

text: Explain (व्याख्या गर्नु), 15 min: invite groups to present, correct misconceptions (clouds move but are not living), then explain biotic and abiotic components and introduce producers (rice plant), consumers (goat), and decomposers (mushroom, bacteria) while drawing a concept map.
source: Exemplar: Components of Environment (reference lesson lp1)
subject: Science

text: Expand (विस्तार गर्नु), 10 min: give the scene 'A rice field contains soil, sunlight, water, rice plants, goats, and mushrooms — classify each' and have students explain why each item is biotic or abiotic and identify producers, consumers, and decomposers.
source: Exemplar: Components of Environment (reference lesson lp1)
subject: Science

text: Evaluate (मूल्याङ्कन गर्नु), 5 min: ask oral questions — What is the environment? Name one biotic and one abiotic component. Which is a producer, consumer, decomposer? Is soil biotic or abiotic and why? — observing participation as the assessment.
source: Exemplar: Components of Environment (reference lesson lp1)
subject: Science

text: Homework (Environment): draw any four things found around your home, write B (Biotic) or A (Abiotic) below each, and for biotic items note whether it is a Producer, Consumer, or Decomposer.
source: Exemplar: Components of Environment (reference lesson lp1)
subject: Science

text: Focused Instruction (I do) (केन्द्रित शिक्षण (म गर्छु)), 8 min: on the board draw a rice-field plot 5 m by 3 m. Think aloud: 'To find the area I multiply length by breadth, 5 x 3 = 15 square metres.' Model the units and write A = l x b, narrating every step so students see an expert's reasoning before they try it.
source: Exemplar: Area of a Rectangle (gradual release reference)
subject: Mathematics

text: Guided Instruction (We do) (निर्देशित अभ्यास (हामी गर्छौं)), 12 min: work two more plots together — a 6 m by 4 m maize field and a 7 m by 2 m vegetable bed. Ask students to call out the numbers, let them decide the operation, and fill the steps together, gradually handing the pen to them and correcting the common slip of adding instead of multiplying.
source: Exemplar: Area of a Rectangle (gradual release reference)
subject: Mathematics

text: Collaborative Learning (You do together) (सहकार्य (तिमीहरू सँगै गर्छौ)), 15 min: in pairs, students measure their desk top and a floor tile with a ruler and compute each area, then compare answers with the pair beside them and resolve any difference by re-checking length x breadth together.
source: Exemplar: Area of a Rectangle (gradual release reference)
subject: Mathematics

text: Independent Practice (You do alone) (स्वतन्त्र अभ्यास (तिमी आफैँ गर्छौ)), 8 min: each student solves three problems alone — a 9 m by 5 m courtyard, an 8 m by 8 m square garden, and a word problem about tiling a 4 m by 3 m kitchen — writing the formula, the working, and the unit for each.
source: Exemplar: Area of a Rectangle (gradual release reference)
subject: Mathematics

text: Homework (Area of a Rectangle): measure the length and breadth of two rectangular objects at home (a mat, a door, a field, a book), record them in metres or centimetres, and calculate the area of each showing A = l x b and the correct square unit.
source: Exemplar: Area of a Rectangle (gradual release reference)
subject: Mathematics

text: Orientation (अभिमुखीकरण), 6 min: show two small pots of soaked black gram (mas) — one that sprouted on the kitchen shelf and one that did not by the window. Ask students what they notice and wonder, letting curiosity build about why one seed woke up and the other stayed asleep.
source: Exemplar: What Seeds Need to Germinate (inquiry reference)
subject: Science

text: Questioning (प्रश्न निर्माण), 8 min: guide students to turn their wonder into investigable questions — 'Do seeds need water to sprout?', 'Do they need warmth?', 'Do they need light?' — and record the class questions on the board, choosing water and warmth to test first.
source: Exemplar: What Seeds Need to Germinate (inquiry reference)
subject: Science

text: Investigation (अनुसन्धान), 16 min: in groups students set up cotton-wool cups of maize or gram seeds under different conditions (dry vs damp, warm shelf vs cold windowsill) and predict, label, and agree to observe them over the coming days, recording their setup in their notebooks.
source: Exemplar: What Seeds Need to Germinate (inquiry reference)
subject: Science

text: Conclusion (निष्कर्ष), 10 min: using an earlier prepared set of cups showing results, groups compare the damp-and-warm seeds (sprouted) with the dry or cold ones (not sprouted) and build the explanation that seeds need water and warmth to germinate, citing their own evidence.
source: Exemplar: What Seeds Need to Germinate (inquiry reference)
subject: Science

text: Reflection & Discussion (चिन्तन र छलफल), 5 min: groups share findings and reflect — how do we know it was water and not light? what would a farmer in the village do before sowing? — connecting the evidence to how they reached their conclusion.
source: Exemplar: What Seeds Need to Germinate (inquiry reference)
subject: Science

text: Homework (Seed Germination): soak five gram or maize seeds in damp cloth at home, keep them warm, and record over three days which day each seed sprouts and how long the shoot grows, noting anything that seemed to help or slow them.
source: Exemplar: What Seeds Need to Germinate (inquiry reference)
subject: Science
